post_meta.author: u/postholepete
post_meta.title: Forester in May, turn around stories
post_meta.text: Attempted Forester 5/26. Deep snow from Tyndall on, navigation entirely on GPS, the chute had no boot pack and we did not like the runout so we turned around and camped. Crampons and axes and we still bailed. The couple behind us kept going, hope they are ok. Tyndall was dangerous at midday, waist deep and fast.

post_meta.author: trailname_Gears
post_meta.title: Forester 6/13
post_meta.text: Forester 6/13 NOBO. Chute had a solid boot pack, axe out for maybe 10 minutes, no big deal. Snow starts around 12,000 on the south side. Tyndall crossing thigh high at 5pm, do it in the morning. Second year on trail, this is way more snow than 2022.

extraction.quote_span: Boot pack all the way up the chute, firm at 5am, axe in hand but never needed it, spikes did the work

post_meta.author: u/postholepete
post_meta.title: Forester round two, success
post_meta.text: Came back for Forester 6/14 after our May bail. Night and day. Boot pack all the way up the chute, firm at 5am, axe in hand but never needed it, spikes did the work. Over the top by 7. Tyndall at dawn was knee high. Patience wins in a big snow year.

post_meta.title: Forester late August
post_meta.text: Forester on the 22nd. Snow free both sides, the chute is dry, Tyndall Creek is ankle deep. August walking. The only conditions note is smoke drifting in from the west in the afternoons.
